chapter: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
title: McShann's postwar band and managers pushing small groups
summary: He rejoined McShann's re-formed big band after the Army, which failed over bookings and managers who pushed small bands.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Even McShann was in the Famous Door there.
Was he?
His band.
Oh? After he came out of the Army, you mean.
After the Army, after the Army.
Yes, with a small band.
No, no, this was a big band, because I even came back to McShann's band after I came out, when he came back to New York.
Right after the both of you came out?
Yeah, when he came out he started the band back again. And I was with him.
Why didn't it stick?
I don't know. I do know, too, because of the bookings. We wasn't getting the right bookings and the right money.
Yeah. It was beginning to be bad for the big bands.
Well, not really. I never thought that.
Didn't you, Gus?
No, because a lot of the time it was the managers that booked the band, you know? Well, they would tell the bandleaders, I can get you the same money for a small band and all like that.
Yeah, oh, I see what you mean, yeah.
That's what I think happened to --
They helped to wreck it.
-- happened to Earl Hines, the reason why his band broke up.
Yes.
We were in the Savoy when that broke up, and so --
